summary: Layer counts from the E2g1–A1g separation (514.5 nm, 285 nm SiO2/Si, Lee 2010 Fig. 2b): B = 1L (Δ 19.2 cm-1), A = 2L (21.4), D = about 4L (24.3, so 4L to a few more layers), and C = bulk-like (25.1, thicker than about 5L and probably much thicker). Two independent observables agree: the Si 520 cm-1 line is progressively attenuated and the Si-normalised MoS2 signal rises in the order B < A < D < C. The spectra are narrow and clean: E2g1 FWHM is about 2.1 cm-1 in all four flakes, with no LA(M) defect band and no 150–650 cm-1 resonant extras. The flakes are therefore good-quality 2H-MoS2 that differ mainly in thickness. A, B and the 1L/2L split are robust. D versus C, and the exact layer number above 4L, are not fixed by this pair of modes. The 1 cm-1 differences in absolute position between flakes (including the E2g1 that sits 0.5 cm-1 higher in B than in A) must not be read as strain or doping without a more careful look.

observations.finding: Flake B is a monolayer. Both modes are weak relative to Si and the A1g is broad.
observations.evidence: Si-corrected E2g1 384.60±0.03 and A1g 403.84±0.10 cm-1, Δ = 19.23±0.10 cm-1 (fit error only; allow about ±0.5 for calibration, resolution and strain/doping). Tabulated 1L is 19.1 cm-1, 2L is 21.4. Relation gives 1L with high confidence. A1g FWHM is 4.75 cm-1 and E2g1 FWHM is 2.04 cm-1. E2g1 height over Si height is 0.40, the lowest of the four.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, ACS Nano 4, 2695, Fig. 2b (arXiv:1005.2509); relation mos2_layer_number_from_separation

observations.evidence: Si-corrected E2g1 384.05±0.02 and A1g 405.47±0.07 cm-1, Δ = 21.43±0.08 cm-1, matching the 2L value of 21.4 and well separated from 1L (19.1) and 3L (23.1). A1g is the broadest of the four (FWHM 6.16 cm-1), which matches the A1g widening toward 2L reported by Lee. E2g1 FWHM is 2.12 cm-1. Si-normalised E2g1 is 0.96.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, Fig. 2b and p.4 (widths)

observations.finding: Flake D is a few-layer flake, about 4L by the separation. Δ saturates here, so 4L to roughly 6L cannot be distinguished.
observations.evidence: Si-corrected E2g1 383.08±0.01 and A1g 407.35±0.03 cm-1, Δ = 24.27±0.03 cm-1 (4L is 24.3, bulk 25.2, a difference of about 0.9 cm-1, comparable to the 2.7 cm-1 resolution). A1g FWHM is 4.45 cm-1, intermediate between A and C. Si is still clearly visible (Si height 940 against E2g1 2574, ratio 2.7), so the flake is thinner than C.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, Fig. 2b; Li et al. arXiv:1308.3835 (Si-normalised intensity increases monotonically with N)

observations.finding: Flake C is bulk-like, at least about 5L and probably tens of nm thick. Its Si line is nearly extinguished.
observations.evidence: Si-corrected E2g1 383.0±0.05 and A1g 408.07±0.06 cm-1, Δ = 25.07±0.08 cm-1 (bulk 25.2). A1g is narrow, FWHM 2.86 cm-1, as expected for bulk. The Si line height is only 74 counts against 334 for E2g1 (Si-normalised E2g1 about 4.5, the highest), and the strongest band is only 19x noise. The relation confidence is only 'moderate'. Thick MoS2 absorbs and attenuates the Si 520 line.
observations.source: Lee et al. 2010, Fig. 2b; Li et al. arXiv:1308.3835

observations.finding: The E2g1 softens and the A1g stiffens from 1L to bulk, which is the standard thickness signature. The four flakes follow it.
observations.evidence: Si-corrected E2g1: B 384.60, A 384.05, D 383.08, C 383.00 cm-1. A1g: B 403.84, A 405.47, D 407.35, C 408.07 cm-1. Separation: 19.2, 21.4, 24.3, 25.1 cm-1. The E2g1 width is constant (2.0–2.1 cm-1) in all flakes.

observations.finding: The crystal quality is good and no defect or resonance bands are seen.
observations.evidence: E2g1 FWHM is 2.04–2.12 cm-1 in all four flakes, essentially the 2.7 cm-1 instrument resolution. LA(M) near 227 cm-1 and the 286 and 471 cm-1 bands are not above noise in any flake (mean counts at 222–232 cm-1 are within a few percent of the adjacent baseline). The Si-normalised signal in A and B is not enhanced by a background. B has only a very broad weak background feature near 222 cm-1 (FWHM about 65 cm-1) that is not a band.
observations.source: Mignuzzi et al. 2015, PRB 91, 195411 (LA(M) as defect band); Lee et al. 2010 (narrow E2g1 indicates a good crystal)

observations.finding: The Si lines indicate the spectrometer reads about 0.7 cm-1 low, and the position scatter between flakes is larger than this correction.
observations.evidence: Si line at 520.02, 520.00, 519.99 cm-1 for A, B, D (offsets -0.68, -0.70, -0.71 cm-1 from 520.7). C's Si line is too weak to calibrate (offset -0.76 with an error of about 0.3 cm-1). The series analysis applies the correction to all peaks. Δ is independent of this offset.

observations.finding: Intensity is consistent with thickness in order, but it is not an independent thickness measure.
observations.evidence: Si-normalised E2g1 height (areas give the same order): B 0.40, A 0.96, D 2.7, C about 4.5.
observations.source: Li et al. arXiv:1308.3835 for the monotonic Si-normalised signal. Absolute intensities depend on interference with the 285 nm SiO2.

properties.name: defect_level
properties.value: low in all four flakes (no LA(M) near 227 cm-1; E2g1 FWHM about 2.1 cm-1)

properties.name: phase
properties.value: 2H (E2g1/A1g pair at 383–385 / 404–408 cm-1; 3R and 1T not tested for in the low-frequency range)

properties.name: strain_sign
properties.value: none established (no E2g1 splitting; shifts are explained by thickness and calibration)
properties.source: Conley 2013, Nano Lett. 13, 3626 (E' splitting under strain)

properties.name: doping_type
properties.value: not determined (A1g position and width tracked thickness; a doping contribution of about 1 cm-1 cannot be excluded)

caveats: The separation threshold between 3L, 4L and bulk is only about 1 cm-1, comparable to the 2.7 cm-1 resolution and to the strain, doping and substrate effects the same table warns about. D is 'about 4L' by the table, but 5–6L or thicker cannot be ruled out. Do not quote a precise layer number for D or C without AFM or the low-frequency modes.

The monolayer/bilayer assignment of B and A rests on the same Δ ruler. Absolute positions are not a thickness measure. B's E2g1 sits 0.56 cm-1 higher than A's, and C's and D's A1g differ by 0.7 cm-1 (about 0.9 cm-1 in Δ); these differences are of the order of the 2.7 cm-1 resolution and the 0.3 cm-1 calibration scatter, so strain or doping is not demonstrated.

In D, the rl_series output lists two very broad bands at about 321 and 330 cm-1 (FWHM about 35 cm-1, position errors of 16–25 cm-1, height errors larger than the heights). These are fit artifacts from baseline curvature, not Raman bands, and should not be assigned (for example to a 'defect' or 'resonant' mode). In B the 222 cm-1 broad feature was likewise ignored. Flake C has one cosmic-ray spike at 265.1 cm-1, which was removed.

Flake C has low signal to noise (strongest band 19x noise), so weak features, including LA(M), would not be visible, and its Si calibration is only about ±0.3 cm-1. Its Δ does not depend on this, but the absolute positions do.

Intensity ratios are strongly affected by interference in the 285 nm SiO2 and by the laser line. The Si-normalised intensity order agrees with thickness but a flake's absolute intensity should not be used to count layers. Optical contrast differences between the flakes are consistent with different thicknesses; they are not an independent proof.

Laser heating: the power at the sample is unknown. Heating redshifts both modes (about -0.012 to -0.016 cm-1/K) and broadens them, and repeated exposure in air can shift A1g by +1.4 and E2g1 by -1 cm-1 (Bera 2017). A single spot per flake was measured, so heating or photo-modification of the thin flakes (especially B and A) cannot be excluded. Multilayer flakes can be thinned by 10 mW at 514 nm (Castellanos-Gomez 2012).

The low-frequency cutoff at 150 cm-1 hides the shear (about 32 cm-1) and layer-breathing modes, which are the proper layer counters above about 4L. The absence of these modes is not evidence of anything.

Alternative for C and D: a thick-flake spectrum can look the same for any N above about 5L. A flake that looks different in the optical microscope could also differ by substrate region (for example a flake edge on bare SiO2 versus on a thicker underlying flake), so a single spot is not necessarily representative of the whole flake.
questions_for_user: What was the laser power at the sample, and was it varied? Heating and photo-annealing shift the modes by about the size of the differences between flakes.
Can you run a polarized pair (XX/YX)? A1g vanishes in crossed polarization while E2g1 stays, which confirms the mode assignment and would show any overlapping feature.
Can you extend the range down to below about 50 cm-1? The shear and breathing modes would separate D from C and fix N for N above 4.
How many spots per flake, and did the spectra vary across each flake? Thickness steps and flake edges are common in exfoliated flakes.
Is there AFM, optical contrast or a reflectance measurement for the same flakes? A single height per flake would calibrate the Δ and intensity rulers directly.
Were the Si line and the laser line calibrated, and is the 0.7 cm-1 low offset the same on all days? C has no usable Si line.

limits: Layer numbers above 4L (flakes D and C) cannot be fixed from the E2g1–A1g pair; only 'about 4 to a few more' (D) and 'at least about 5L' (C) are supported.

The relation is calibrated for exfoliated 2H-MoS2 on 285 nm SiO2/Si at 514.5 nm, which matches this sample. It does not account for strain, doping or heating, so assignments of 1L/2L carry about ±0.5 cm-1 uncertainty in Δ.
The data cannot separate strain, doping, heating and calibration effects on the 1 cm-1 position differences, because there is a single spectrum per flake, no polarization series and no power series.

The data cannot tell the stacking (2H vs 3R) of A, B and D, because the shear and breathing modes below 150 cm-1 are not covered. The E2g1/A1g pair does not distinguish 2H from 3R bilayers (Ranjuna 2023).
The data cannot give thickness in nm; the thickness of C is only a lower bound from the Si attenuation.

The literature positions in Lee 2010 (bulk E2g1 382.2 cm-1) are on a different calibration from the Si-corrected positions here (bulk E2g1 about 383.0 cm-1), so only differences (Δ) were compared, not absolute positions.
The only literature checks done were against the curated MoS2 note and relations (the Lee 2010 Fig. 2b table); the figures of the cited papers were not independently re-read here.
